questions.question: Given that the determinant of the matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & 0\\ 2 & 6 & 4\\ -1 & 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] is -12, the determinant of the matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 6 & 0\\ 4 & 12 & 8\\ -2 & 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
questions.explanation: Let D=-12 for the given matrix [latex] |A|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}2 & 6 & 0 \\4 & 12 & 8 \\-2 & 0 & 4\end{array}\right|=(2)^{3}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 3 & 0 \\2 & 6 & 4 \\-1 & 0 & 2\end{array}\right| [/latex] (Taking 2 common from each row) [latex] \begin{aligned}\therefore \text{Det}(A) &=(2)^{3} \times D \\=& 8 x-12=-96\end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Let D=-12 for the given matrix
[latex] |A|=\left|\begin{array}{ccc}2 & 6 & 0 \\4 & 12 & 8 \\-2 & 0 & 4\end{array}\right|=(2)^{3}\left|\begin{array}{ccc}1 & 3 & 0 \\2 & 6 & 4 \\-1 & 0 & 2\end{array}\right| [/latex]
(Taking 2 common from each row)
[latex] \begin{aligned}\therefore \text{Det}(A) &=(2)^{3} \times D \\=& 8 x-12=-96\end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: [latex]\lim_{x\rightarrow 0} \frac{x-\sin x}{1-\cos x}[/latex] is

questions.question: The integral [latex]\oint_c (ydx-xdy)[/latex]  is evalulated along the circle [latex]x^{2}+y^{2}=\frac{1}{4}[/latex] traversed in counter clockwise direction. The integral is equal to

questions.question: If [latex]y=f(x)[/latex]  is the solution of [latex]\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=0[/latex] with the boundary conditions y=5 at x=0, and  [latex]\frac{dy}{dx}=2[/latex] at x=10, f(15)=_____
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}} &=0 \\ \frac{d y}{d x} &=C_{1} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad C_{1} &=2 \\ y &=C_{1} x+C_{2} \\ at \qquad x &=0 ; \quad y=5=C_{2} \\ \therefore \qquad y &=2 x+5 \\ at \qquad y(15) &=2 \times 15+5=35 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: One of the eigenvectors of the matrix  [latex]\begin{bmatrix} -5 & 2\\ -9 & 6 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]  is
questions.explanation: The characteristic equation [latex] | A-\lambda D=0 [/latex] [latex] \text{i.e.} \left|\begin{array}{cc}-5-\lambda & 2 \\ -9 & 6-\lambda\end{array}\right|=0 [/latex] [latex] \text{or } (\lambda-6)(\lambda+5)+18=0 [/latex] [latex] \text{or } \quad \lambda^{2}-6 \lambda+5 \lambda-30+18=0 [/latex] [latex] \text{or } \quad \lambda^{2}-\lambda-12=0 [/latex] [latex] \text{or } \lambda=\frac{1 \pm \sqrt{1+48}}{2}=\frac{1 \pm 7}{2}=4,-3 [/latex] Corresponding to [latex] \lambda=4,[/latex] we have [latex] \; [A-\lambda I] x=\left[\begin{array}{cc}-5-\lambda & 2 \\-9 & 6-\lambda\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\y\end{array}\right] [/latex] [latex] =0 [/latex] [latex] \text{Or, } \left[\begin{array}{ll}-9 & 2 \\ -9 & 2\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\ y\end{array}\right]=0[/latex]which gives only one independent equation, [latex] -9 x+2 y=0 [/latex] [latex] \therefore \frac{x}{2}=\frac{y}{9}[/latex] gives eigen vector (2,9) Corresponding to [latex] \lambda=-3, [/latex] [latex] =\left[\begin{array}{ll}-2 & 2 \\-9 & 9\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\y \end{array}\right]=0[/latex] which gives -x+y=0 (only one independent equation) [latex] \therefore \quad \frac{x}{1}=\frac{y}{1} \quad [/latex] which gives (1,1) So, the eigen vectors are [latex]\left\{\begin{array}{l}2 \\ 9\end{array}\right\} and \left\{\begin{array}{l}1 \\ 1\end{array}\right\}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
The characteristic equation [latex] | A-\lambda D=0 [/latex]
[latex] \text{i.e.} \left|\begin{array}{cc}-5-\lambda & 2 \\ -9 & 6-\lambda\end{array}\right|=0 [/latex]
[latex] \text{or } (\lambda-6)(\lambda+5)+18=0 [/latex]
[latex] \text{or } \quad \lambda^{2}-6 \lambda+5 \lambda-30+18=0 [/latex]
[latex] \text{or } \quad \lambda^{2}-\lambda-12=0 [/latex]
[latex] \text{or } \lambda=\frac{1 \pm \sqrt{1+48}}{2}=\frac{1 \pm 7}{2}=4,-3 [/latex]
Corresponding to [latex] \lambda=4,[/latex] we have
[latex] \; [A-\lambda I] x=\left[\begin{array}{cc}-5-\lambda & 2 \\-9 & 6-\lambda\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\y\end{array}\right] [/latex]
[latex] =0 [/latex]
[latex] \text{Or, } \left[\begin{array}{ll}-9 & 2 \\ -9 & 2\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\ y\end{array}\right]=0[/latex]which gives only one independent equation,
[latex] -9 x+2 y=0 [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \frac{x}{2}=\frac{y}{9}[/latex] gives eigen vector (2,9)
Corresponding to [latex] \lambda=-3, [/latex]
[latex] =\left[\begin{array}{ll}-2 & 2 \\-9 & 9\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x \\y \end{array}\right]=0[/latex]
which gives -x+y=0 (only one independent equation)
[latex] \therefore \quad \frac{x}{1}=\frac{y}{1} \quad [/latex] which gives (1,1)
So, the eigen vectors are [latex]\left\{\begin{array}{l}2 \\ 9\end{array}\right\} and \left\{\begin{array}{l}1 \\ 1\end{array}\right\}[/latex]

questions.question: Curl of vector [latex]\vec{F}=x^{2}z^{2}\hat{i}-2xy^{2}z\hat{j}+2y^{2}z^{3}\hat{k}[/latex]  is
questions.explanation: [latex]\vec{F}=x^{2} z^{2} \hat{i}-2 x y^{2} z \hat{j}+2 y^{2} z^{3} \hat{k} [/latex] [latex] \nabla \times \vec{F}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ x^{2} z^{2}&-2 x y^{2} z^{2} & 2 y^{2} z^{3} \end{array}\right| [/latex] [latex] =\hat{i}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(2 y^{2} z^{3}\right)+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(2 x y^{2} z\right)\right] [/latex] [latex] -\hat{j}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(2 y^{2} z^{3}\right)-\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(x^{2} z^{2}\right)\right] [/latex] [latex] +\hat{k}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(-2 x y^{2} z\right)-\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(x^{2} z^{2}\right)\right] [/latex] [latex] \nabla \times \vec{F}=\hat{i}\left[4 y z^{3}+2 x y^{2}\right]-\hat{j}\left[-2 z x^{2}\right] [/latex] [latex] =\left(4 y z^{3}+2 x y^{2}\right) \hat{i}+\left(2 x^{2} z\right) \hat{j}-\left(2 y^{2} z\right) \hat{k}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\vec{F}=x^{2} z^{2} \hat{i}-2 x y^{2} z \hat{j}+2 y^{2} z^{3} \hat{k} [/latex]
[latex] \nabla \times \vec{F}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ x^{2} z^{2}&-2 x y^{2} z^{2} & 2 y^{2} z^{3} \end{array}\right| [/latex]
[latex] =\hat{i}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(2 y^{2} z^{3}\right)+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(2 x y^{2} z\right)\right] [/latex]
[latex] -\hat{j}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(2 y^{2} z^{3}\right)-\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(x^{2} z^{2}\right)\right] [/latex]
[latex] +\hat{k}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(-2 x y^{2} z\right)-\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(x^{2} z^{2}\right)\right] [/latex]
[latex] \nabla \times \vec{F}=\hat{i}\left[4 y z^{3}+2 x y^{2}\right]-\hat{j}\left[-2 z x^{2}\right] [/latex]
[latex] =\left(4 y z^{3}+2 x y^{2}\right) \hat{i}+\left(2 x^{2} z\right) \hat{j}-\left(2 y^{2} z\right) \hat{k}[/latex]

questions.question: An analytic function of a complex variable [latex]z=x+iy[/latex] is expressed as  [latex]f(z)=u(x,y)+i v(x,y)[/latex] , where [latex]i=\sqrt{-1}[/latex]. If [latex]u(x,y)=2xy[/latex], then [latex]v(x,y)[/latex] must be
questions.explanation: As per Cauchy-Riemann equation [latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}[/latex] [latex] \text { and } \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} =-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} [/latex] [latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=2 y [/latex] [latex] \text { and } \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 x [/latex] [latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial y}=2 y [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad v=y^{2}+f(x) [/latex] [latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=0+P(x)=-2 x [/latex] [latex] \therefore f(x)=-x^{2}+ \text{constant} [/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad v=y^{2}-x^{2}+ \text{constant}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
As per Cauchy-Riemann equation
[latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}[/latex]
[latex] \text { and } \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} =-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=2 y [/latex]
[latex] \text { and } \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 x [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial y}=2 y [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad v=y^{2}+f(x) [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=0+P(x)=-2 x [/latex]
[latex] \therefore f(x)=-x^{2}+ \text{constant} [/latex]

questions.question: An analytic function of a complex variable [latex]z=x+iy[/latex]  is expressed as [latex]f(z)=u(x,y)+iv(x,y)[/latex]  , where [latex]i=\sqrt{-1}[/latex]. If [latex]u(x,y)=x^{2}-y^{2}[/latex], then expression for [latex]v(x,y)[/latex]  in terms of x, y and a general constant c would be
questions.explanation: As per Cauchy-Riemann equations: [latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} and \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} [/latex] [latex] u=x^{2}-y^{2} [/latex] [latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=2 x, \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-2 y [/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 x [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad v=2 x y+f(x) [/latex] [latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 y+f(x) [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 y+f^{\prime}(x) [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=0 \quad \text { i.e. } f(x)=c [/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad v=2 x y+c [/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
As per Cauchy-Riemann equations:
[latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} and \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} [/latex]
[latex] u=x^{2}-y^{2} [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=2 x, \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-2 y [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 x [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad v=2 x y+f(x) [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 y+f(x) [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 y+f^{\prime}(x) [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=0 \quad \text { i.e. } f(x)=c [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad v=2 x y+c [/latex]

questions.question: Consider two solutions [latex]x(t)=x_{1}(t)[/latex] and  [latex]x(t)=x_{2}(t)[/latex]  of the differential equation [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d}^2x(t)}{\mathrm{d} t^{2}}+x(t)=0,\; t\gt 0[/latex]  , such that [latex]x_{1}(0)=1,\; \frac{\mathrm{d}x_{1}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t}|_{t=0} =0,x_{2}(0)=0,\frac{\mathrm{d}x_{2}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t}|_{t=0} =1[/latex]  . The wronskian [latex]W(t)=\begin{vmatrix} x_{1}(t) & x_{2}(t)\\ \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{1}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t} & \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{2}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t} \end{vmatrix}[/latex]  at [latex]t=\pi /2[/latex]  is.
questions.explanation: Given differential equation in symbolic form is [latex] \left(D^{2}+1\right) x(t)=0 [/latex] Its A.E. is [latex] D^{2}+1=0 [/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad D=\pm i [/latex] So, C.F. is [latex] x_{1}(t)=C_{1} \cos t [/latex] [latex] x_{2}(t)=C_{2} \sin t[/latex] [latex] \therefore x_{1}(0)=C_{1}=1 [/latex] [latex] \begin{array}{l} \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad x_{1}(t) &=\operatorname{cost} \\ \text { it satisfies }\left.\begin{matrix} \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{1}(t)}{d t}\end{matrix} \right|_{t=0} &=0 \end{aligned} \\ \qquad \begin{aligned} x_{2}(0) &=0=C_{2} \sin (0)\left(\because C_{2} \neq 0\right) \\ \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t} &=C_{2} \cos t \end{aligned} \\ \left.\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t}\right|_{t=0}=C_{2}=1 \end{array}[/latex] [latex] \begin{array}{l} \therefore  \;\; x_{2}(t)=\sin t \\ W(t)= \begin{vmatrix} x_{1}(t) & x_{2}(t) \\ \frac{d x_{1}(t)}{d t} & \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t}\end{vmatrix}= \begin{vmatrix} \cos t & \sin t \\ -\sin t & \cos t \end{vmatrix} \\ M(t)=\cos ^{2} t+\sin ^{2} t=1 \end{array}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given differential equation in symbolic form is
[latex] \left(D^{2}+1\right) x(t)=0 [/latex]
Its A.E. is [latex] D^{2}+1=0 [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad D=\pm i [/latex]
So, C.F. is
[latex] x_{1}(t)=C_{1} \cos t [/latex]
[latex] x_{2}(t)=C_{2} \sin t[/latex]
[latex] \therefore x_{1}(0)=C_{1}=1 [/latex]
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad x_{1}(t) &=\operatorname{cost} \\ \text { it satisfies }\left.\begin{matrix} \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{1}(t)}{d t}\end{matrix} \right|_{t=0} &=0 \end{aligned} \\ \qquad \begin{aligned} x_{2}(0) &=0=C_{2} \sin (0)\left(\because C_{2} \neq 0\right) \\ \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t} &=C_{2} \cos t \end{aligned} \\ \left.\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t}\right|_{t=0}=C_{2}=1 \end{array}[/latex]
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \therefore \;\; x_{2}(t)=\sin t \\ W(t)= \begin{vmatrix} x_{1}(t) & x_{2}(t) \\ \frac{d x_{1}(t)}{d t} & \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t}\end{vmatrix}= \begin{vmatrix} \cos t & \sin t \\ -\sin t & \cos t \end{vmatrix} \\ M(t)=\cos ^{2} t+\sin ^{2} t=1 \end{array}[/latex]

questions.question: A machine produces 0, 1 or 2 defective pieces in a day with associated probability of 1/6, 2/3 and 1/6, respectively. The mean value and the variance of the number of defective pieces produced by the machine in a day,  respectively, are
questions.explanation: [latex] \begin{aligned} \operatorname{mean} &=\Sigma x \cdot p(x)=0\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)+1\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+2\left(\frac{1}{6}\right) \\ &=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{6}=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{3}{3}=1 \\ E\left(x^{2}\right) &=0\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)+1\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+4\left(\frac{1}{6}\right) \\ &=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{3} \\ \text { Variance } &=E\left(x^{2}\right)-\left(E(x)^{2}\right)=\frac{4}{3}-1=\frac{1}{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex] \begin{aligned} \operatorname{mean} &=\Sigma x \cdot p(x)=0\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)+1\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+2\left(\frac{1}{6}\right) \\ &=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{6}=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{3}{3}=1 \\ E\left(x^{2}\right) &=0\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)+1\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+4\left(\frac{1}{6}\right) \\ &=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{3} \\ \text { Variance } &=E\left(x^{2}\right)-\left(E(x)^{2}\right)=\frac{4}{3}-1=\frac{1}{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: The real root of the equation [latex]5x-2cosx-1=0[/latex]  (up to two decimal accuracy) is _______
questions.explanation: [latex]f(x)=5 x-2 \cos x-1 [/latex] [latex] f(x)=5+2 \sin x [/latex] By Newton Raphson's equation: [latex] x_{n+1}=x_{n}-\frac{f\left(x_{n}\right)}{f^{\prime}\left(x_{n}\right)} [/latex] Assuming [latex] x_{0}=1 \quad\left(1 \text{ rad}=57.32^{\circ}\right) [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad x_{1}=1-\frac{5 \times 1-2 \cos \left(57.32^{\circ}\right)-1}{5+2 \sin \left(57.32^{\circ}\right)}=0.5632 [/latex] Again, [latex] x_{2}=0.5632-\frac{5 \times 0.5632-2 \cos \left(32.27^{\circ}\right)-1}{5+2 \sin \left(32.27^{\circ}\right)} [/latex] [latex] =0.5425 [/latex] [latex] \begin{aligned} x_{3} &=0.5425-\frac{5 \times 0.5425-2 \cos \left(31.09^{\circ}\right)-1}{5+2 \sin \left(31.09^{\circ}\right)} \\ &=0.5424 \end{aligned} [/latex] [latex] \therefore [/latex] Real root, x=0.54

By Newton Raphson's equation:
[latex] x_{n+1}=x_{n}-\frac{f\left(x_{n}\right)}{f^{\prime}\left(x_{n}\right)} [/latex]
Assuming [latex] x_{0}=1 \quad\left(1 \text{ rad}=57.32^{\circ}\right) [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad x_{1}=1-\frac{5 \times 1-2 \cos \left(57.32^{\circ}\right)-1}{5+2 \sin \left(57.32^{\circ}\right)}=0.5632 [/latex]
Again,
[latex] x_{2}=0.5632-\frac{5 \times 0.5632-2 \cos \left(32.27^{\circ}\right)-1}{5+2 \sin \left(32.27^{\circ}\right)} [/latex]
[latex] =0.5425 [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} x_{3} &=0.5425-\frac{5 \times 0.5425-2 \cos \left(31.09^{\circ}\right)-1}{5+2 \sin \left(31.09^{\circ}\right)} \\ &=0.5424 \end{aligned} [/latex]

questions.question: The value of the integral [latex]\int_{0}^{2}\frac{(x-1)^{2}\sin(x-1)}{(x-1)^{2}+\cos(x-1)}dx[/latex] is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} I &= \int_{0}^{2}\frac{(x-1)^2 \sin (x-1)}{(x-1)^2 + \cos (x-1)}dx\\ \text{Taking}\; x-1=z&\Rightarrow dx=dz \\ \text{for}\; x=0,&z\rightarrow -1\; \text{and}\; x=2, z \rightarrow 1 \\ \therefore \; I &=\int_{-1}^{1} \frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+\cos z}dz\\ \text{let}\;\; f(z)&=\frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+ \cos z} dz\\ f(-z) &= \frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+ \cos z}\\ f(z)&= -f(z) \; \text{function is ODD}\\ \therefore \;\; I&=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} I &= \int_{0}^{2}\frac{(x-1)^2 \sin (x-1)}{(x-1)^2 + \cos (x-1)}dx\\ \text{Taking}\; x-1=z&\Rightarrow dx=dz \\ \text{for}\; x=0,&z\rightarrow -1\; \text{and}\; x=2, z \rightarrow 1 \\ \therefore \; I &=\int_{-1}^{1} \frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+\cos z}dz\\ \text{let}\;\; f(z)&=\frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+ \cos z} dz\\ f(-z) &= \frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+ \cos z}\\ f(z)&= -f(z) \; \text{function is ODD}\\ \therefore \;\; I&=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: The number of accidents occurring in a plant in a month follows Poisson distribution with mean as 5.2. The probability of occurrence of less than 2 accidents in the plant during a randomly selected month is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} P(x) &=\frac{\mu^{x} \mathrm{e}^{-\mu}}{x !} \\ P(x \lt 2) &=P(0)+P(1) \\ &=\frac{\mu^{0} e^{-\mu}}{0 !}+\frac{\mu^{1} e^{-\mu}}{1 !} \\ &=\frac{1}{e^{\mu}}+\frac{\mu}{e^{\mu}}=\frac{1+\mu}{e^{\mu}} \\ \operatorname{As} \mu(\operatorname{mean})=5 & \cdot 2 \\ \therefore \quad P(x \lt 2) &=\frac{6.2}{e^{5.2}}=0.0342 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A block weighing 200 N is in contact with a level plane whose coefficients of static and kinetic friction are 0.4 and 0.2, respectively. questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} N &=m g=200 \mathrm{N} \\(f_{s})_{max} &=\mu_{s} N \\ &=0.4 \times 200=80 \end{aligned}[/latex] upto [latex] 8 \sec [P=10 t] \rightarrow [/latex] no motion [latex] \Rightarrow [/latex] from 8 sec to 10 sec [latex] \begin{aligned} f_{k} &=\mu_{k} N \\ &=0.2 \times 200=40 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned} [/latex] Average applied force [latex] =\frac{P_{\max }+P_{\min }}{2} [/latex] [latex] =\frac{100+80}{2}=90 \mathrm{N}[/latex] Average resultant force = Avg. applied force kinetic friction [latex] =90-40=50 N[/latex] Average acceration [latex] \begin{aligned} &=\frac{50 \times 9.8}{200} \\ \Rightarrow \quad V &=u+a t\\ u&=0\\ a&=\frac{50 \times 9.8}{200} \\ t&=2 \text{second}\\ \therefore V&=\frac{50 \times 9.8}{200} \times 2=4.9 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A rigid uniform rod AB of length L and mass m is hinged at C such that AC = L/3, CB = 2L/3. Ends A and B are supported by springs of spring constant k. The natural frequency of the system is given by

questions.question: 1.5 kg of water is in saturated liquid state at 2 bar ([latex]v_{f}= 0.001061 m^3/kg[/latex], [latex]u_{f}[/latex]=504.0 kJ/kg,  [latex]h_{f}[/latex]=505 kJ/kg). Heat is added in a constant pressure process till the temperature of water reaches 400[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C  (v=1.5493 [latex]m^3[/latex]/kg, u = 2967.0 kJ/kg, h = 3277.0 kJ/kg). The heat added (in kJ) in the process is  _______
questions.explanation: From the first law of thermodynamics [latex] \begin{aligned} \delta q &=d u+p d v \\ \delta q &=\left(u_{2}-u_{1}\right)+p\left(v_{2}-v_{1}\right) \\ \delta q &=(2967-504)+2 \times 10^{2} \\ &(1.5493-0.001061) \\ \delta q &=2463+309.6478 \\ &=2772.6478 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex] For 1.5kg of water [latex] \begin{aligned} Q &=2772.6478 \times 1.5 \\ &=4158.97 \mathrm{kj} \end{aligned}[/latex] Alternatively: [latex] \begin{aligned} Q &=m\left(h_{2}-h_{1}\right) \\ &=1.5(3277-505) \\ &=4158 \mathrm{kJ} \end{aligned}[/latex]

From the first law of thermodynamics
[latex] \begin{aligned} \delta q &=d u+p d v \\ \delta q &=\left(u_{2}-u_{1}\right)+p\left(v_{2}-v_{1}\right) \\ \delta q &=(2967-504)+2 \times 10^{2} \\ &(1.5493-0.001061) \\ \delta q &=2463+309.6478 \\ &=2772.6478 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For 1.5kg of water

Alternatively:
[latex] \begin{aligned} Q &=m\left(h_{2}-h_{1}\right) \\ &=1.5(3277-505) \\ &=4158 \mathrm{kJ} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: Consider one dimensional steady state heat conduction across a wall (as shown in figure below) of thickness 30 mm and thermal conductivity 15 W/m.K. At x = 0, a constant heat flux, [latex]q''= 1\times 10^5 W/m^2[/latex]  is applied. On the other side of the wall, heat is removed from the wall by convection with a fluid at 25[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and heat transfer coefficient of 250 [latex]W/m^2[/latex] K. The temperature  (in [latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C), at x = 0 is _______
questions.explanation: Given data: [latex] \begin{aligned} \delta&=30 \mathrm{mm}=0.03 \mathrm{m} ; \quad k=15 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} \\ q^{\prime \prime}&=1 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} ; \quad T_{\infty}=25^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ h&=250 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex] Heat transfer due to convection from outside surface per unit area: [latex] \begin{aligned} q^{\prime \prime} &=\frac{Q}{A}=h\left(T_{2}-T_{\infty}\right) \\ 1 \times 10^{5} &=250\left(T_{2}-25\right) \\ \text{or}\qquad T_{2} &=425^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}[/latex] Heat transfer through wall per unit area, [latex] \begin{aligned} q^{\prime \prime} &=\frac{k\left(T_{1}-T_{2}\right)}{\delta} \\ 1 \times 10^{5} &=\frac{15\left(T_{1}-425\right)}{0.03}\\ \text{or }\qquad T_{1}&=625^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: Water flows through a pipe having an inner radius of 10 mm at the rate of 36 kg/hr at 25[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C.  The viscosity of water at 25[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C is 0.001 kg/m.s.  The Reynolds number of the flow is _______
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Radius: }\quad r&=10 \mathrm{mm} \\ \therefore \text{Diameter: }d&=2 r=2 \times 10=20 \mathrm{mm}=0.02 \mathrm{m} \\ m &=36 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{hr}=\frac{36}{3600}=0.01 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ \mu &=0.001 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{ms} \end{aligned}[/latex] Reynolds number: [latex]\text{Re}=\frac{\rho V d}{\mu}[/latex] From continuity equation, [latex]m=\rho A V [/latex] [latex] \begin{aligned} \text{or }\quad V&=\frac{m}{\rho A}=\frac{m}{\frac{\rho \pi d^{2}}{4}}=\frac{4 m}{\rho \pi d^{2}} \\ \therefore \quad \mathrm{Re}&=\frac{\rho d}{\mu} \times \frac{4 \mathrm{m}}{\rho \pi d^{2}}=\frac{4 \mathrm{m}}{\pi \mu \mathrm{d}}\\ &=\frac{4 \times 0.01}{3.14 \times 0.001 \times 0.02}=636.94 \end{aligned}[/latex]

Reynolds number: [latex]\text{Re}=\frac{\rho V d}{\mu}[/latex]
From continuity equation, [latex]m=\rho A V [/latex]

questions.question: The non-dimensional fluid temperature profile near the surface of a convectively cooled flat plate is given by [latex]\frac{T_W-T}{T_W-T_\infty }=a+b\frac{y}{L}+c\left ( \frac{y}{L} \right )^2[/latex], where y is measured perpendicular to the plate, [latex]L[/latex]  is the plate length, and a, b and c are arbitrary constants. [latex]T_{W}[/latex]  and [latex]T_{\infty}[/latex]  are wall and ambient temperatures, respectively. If the thermal conductivity of the fluid is [latex]k[/latex]   and the wall heat flux is [latex]q''[/latex], the Nusselt number [latex]N_u=\frac{q''}{T_W-T_\infty }\frac{L}{k}[/latex]  is  equal to
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} q^{\prime \prime} &=-\left.k \frac{\partial T}{\partial y}\right|_{y=0} \\ &=h\left(T_{w}-T_{\infty}\right) \\ T_{w}-T &=\left(T_{w}-T_{\infty}\right)\left[a+\frac{b y}{L}+c\left(\frac{y}{L}\right)^{2}\right] \\ \frac{\partial T}{\partial y} & =\left(T_{w}-T_{\infty}\right)\left[\frac{b}{L}+\frac{2 c}{L^{2}} y\right] \\ -\left.\frac{\partial T}{\partial y}\right|_{y=0} &=\left(T_{w}-T_{\infty}\right) \frac{b}{L} \\ \text{or} \quad q^{\prime \prime}&=k\left(T_{w}-T_{\infty}\right) \frac{b}{L} \\ \therefore \quad N u &=\frac{q^{\prime \prime}}{T_{w}-T_{\infty}} \frac{L}{k}=b \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: In an air-standard Otto cycle, air is supplied at 0.1 MPa and 308 K. The ratio of the specific heats ([latex]\gamma[/latex] ) and the specific gas constant (R) of air are 1.4 and 288.8 J/kg.K, respectively. If the compression ratio is 8 and the maximum temperature in the cycle is 2660 K, the heat (in kJ/kg) supplied to the engine is _______
questions.explanation:
Given: [latex] \begin{aligned} p_{1}&=0.1 \mathrm{MPa} ; \quad T_{1}=308 \mathrm{K} ; \quad \gamma=1.4 \\ R&=288.8 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} ; \quad r=8 \\ T_{s}&=2660 \mathrm{K} \\ &\begin{aligned} Q_{s}&=m c_{v}\left(T_{3}-T_{2}\right) \\ c_{v}&=\frac{R}{\gamma-1}=\frac{288.8}{0.4}=722 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}&=\left(\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}\right)^{\gamma-1}=(8)^{0.4}\\
T_{2} &=308 \times 8^{0.4}=707.6 \mathrm{K} \\
Q_{s} &=m c_{v} \Delta T \\
&=1 \times 722(2660-707.6) \\
&=1409.6 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}[/latex]

Given:
[latex] \begin{aligned} p_{1}&=0.1 \mathrm{MPa} ; \quad T_{1}=308 \mathrm{K} ; \quad \gamma=1.4 \\ R&=288.8 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} ; \quad r=8 \\ T_{s}&=2660 \mathrm{K} \\ &\begin{aligned} Q_{s}&=m c_{v}\left(T_{3}-T_{2}\right) \\ c_{v}&=\frac{R}{\gamma-1}=\frac{288.8}{0.4}=722 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}&=\left(\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}\right)^{\gamma-1}=(8)^{0.4}\\ T_{2} &=308 \times 8^{0.4}=707.6 \mathrm{K} \\ Q_{s} &=m c_{v} \Delta T \\ &=1 \times 722(2660-707.6) \\ &=1409.6 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A reversible heat engine receives 2 kJ of heat from a reservoir at 1000 K and a certain amount of heat from a reservoir at 800 K. It rejects 1 kJ of heat to a reservoir at 400 K. The network output (in kJ) of the cycle is
questions.explanation: For reversible heat engine, [latex]\begin{aligned} (\Delta S)_{\text{ Reversible cycle }}&=0\\ \frac{Q_1}{T_1}+\frac{Q_2}{T_2}-\frac{Q_3}{T_3}&=0\\ \frac{2}{1000}+\frac{Q_2}{800}-\frac{1}{400}&=0\\ Q_2&=0.4 kJ\\ \text{From heat balance, }\\ Q_1+Q_2&=W+Q_3\\ 2+0.4&=W+1\\ W&=1.4 kJ \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.topic: Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy
questions.explanation_html:
For reversible heat engine,
[latex]\begin{aligned} (\Delta S)_{\text{ Reversible cycle }}&=0\\ \frac{Q_1}{T_1}+\frac{Q_2}{T_2}-\frac{Q_3}{T_3}&=0\\ \frac{2}{1000}+\frac{Q_2}{800}-\frac{1}{400}&=0\\ Q_2&=0.4 kJ\\ \text{From heat balance, }\\ Q_1+Q_2&=W+Q_3\\ 2+0.4&=W+1\\ W&=1.4 kJ \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: An ideal reheat Rankine cycle operates between the pressure limits of 10 kPa and 8 MPa, with reheat being done at 4 MPa. The temperature of steam at the inlets of both turbines is 500[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and the enthalpy of steam is 3185 kJ/kg at the exit of the high pressure turbine and 2247 kJ/kg at the exit of low pressure turbine. The enthalpy of water at the exit from the pump is 191 kJ/kg. Use the following table for relevant data. Disregarding the pump work, the cycle efficiency (in percentage) is __________
questions.explanation: Given [latex] \begin{aligned} p_{2} &=10 \mathrm{kPa} ; \quad p_{1}=8 \mathrm{MPa} \\ p_{3} &=4 \mathrm{MPa} ; \quad h_{2}=3185 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{4} &=2247 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} ; \quad h_{1}=3399 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{3} &=3446 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} ; \quad h_{6}=191 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ w_{\mathrm{T}} &=\left(h_{1}-h_{2}\right)+\left(h_{3}-h_{4}\right) \\ q_{s} &=\left(h_{1}-h_{6}\right)+\left(h_{3}-h_{2}\right) \\ \therefore \quad w_{T} &=(3399-3185)+(3446-2247) \\ &=1413 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ q_{\mathrm{s}} &=(3399-191)+(3446-3185) \\ &=3469 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ \eta &=\frac{w_{\mathrm{T}}}{q_{\mathrm{s}}}=\frac{1413}{3469}=0.4073 \\ &=40.73 \% \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given
[latex] \begin{aligned} p_{2} &=10 \mathrm{kPa} ; \quad p_{1}=8 \mathrm{MPa} \\ p_{3} &=4 \mathrm{MPa} ; \quad h_{2}=3185 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{4} &=2247 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} ; \quad h_{1}=3399 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{3} &=3446 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} ; \quad h_{6}=191 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ w_{\mathrm{T}} &=\left(h_{1}-h_{2}\right)+\left(h_{3}-h_{4}\right) \\ q_{s} &=\left(h_{1}-h_{6}\right)+\left(h_{3}-h_{2}\right) \\ \therefore \quad w_{T} &=(3399-3185)+(3446-2247) \\ &=1413 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ q_{\mathrm{s}} &=(3399-191)+(3446-3185) \\ &=3469 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ \eta &=\frac{w_{\mathrm{T}}}{q_{\mathrm{s}}}=\frac{1413}{3469}=0.4073 \\ &=40.73 \% \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A metal rod of initial length [latex]L_{0}[/latex]  is subjected to a drawing process. questions.question: Curl of vector [latex]\vec{F}=x^{2}z^{2}\hat{i}-2xy^{2}z\hat{j}+2y^{2}z^{3}\hat{k}[/latex]  is
questions.explanation: [latex]\vec{F}=x^{2} z^{2} \hat{i}-2 x y^{2} z \hat{j}+2 y^{2} z^{3} \hat{k} [/latex] [latex] \nabla \times \vec{F}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ x^{2} z^{2}&-2 x y^{2} z^{2} & 2 y^{2} z^{3} \end{array}\right| [/latex] [latex] =\hat{i}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(2 y^{2} z^{3}\right)+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(2 x y^{2} z\right)\right] [/latex] [latex] -\hat{j}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(2 y^{2} z^{3}\right)-\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(x^{2} z^{2}\right)\right] [/latex] [latex] +\hat{k}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(-2 x y^{2} z\right)-\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(x^{2} z^{2}\right)\right] [/latex] [latex] \nabla \times \vec{F}=\hat{i}\left[4 y z^{3}+2 x y^{2}\right]-\hat{j}\left[-2 z x^{2}\right] [/latex] [latex] =\left(4 y z^{3}+2 x y^{2}\right) \hat{i}+\left(2 x^{2} z\right) \hat{j}-\left(2 y^{2} z\right) \hat{k}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\vec{F}=x^{2} z^{2} \hat{i}-2 x y^{2} z \hat{j}+2 y^{2} z^{3} \hat{k} [/latex]
[latex] \nabla \times \vec{F}=\left|\begin{array}{ccc} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial}{\partial z} \\ x^{2} z^{2}&-2 x y^{2} z^{2} & 2 y^{2} z^{3} \end{array}\right| [/latex]
[latex] =\hat{i}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(2 y^{2} z^{3}\right)+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(2 x y^{2} z\right)\right] [/latex]
[latex] -\hat{j}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(2 y^{2} z^{3}\right)-\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(x^{2} z^{2}\right)\right] [/latex]
[latex] +\hat{k}\left[\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(-2 x y^{2} z\right)-\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(x^{2} z^{2}\right)\right] [/latex]
[latex] \nabla \times \vec{F}=\hat{i}\left[4 y z^{3}+2 x y^{2}\right]-\hat{j}\left[-2 z x^{2}\right] [/latex]
[latex] =\left(4 y z^{3}+2 x y^{2}\right) \hat{i}+\left(2 x^{2} z\right) \hat{j}-\left(2 y^{2} z\right) \hat{k}[/latex]

questions.explanation: As per Cauchy-Riemann equation [latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}[/latex] [latex] \text { and } \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} =-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} [/latex] [latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=2 y [/latex] [latex] \text { and } \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 x [/latex] [latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial y}=2 y [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad v=y^{2}+f(x) [/latex] [latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=0+P(x)=-2 x [/latex] [latex] \therefore f(x)=-x^{2}+ \text{constant} [/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad v=y^{2}-x^{2}+ \text{constant}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
As per Cauchy-Riemann equation
[latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y}[/latex]
[latex] \text { and } \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} =-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=2 y [/latex]
[latex] \text { and } \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 x [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial y}=2 y [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad v=y^{2}+f(x) [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=0+P(x)=-2 x [/latex]
[latex] \therefore f(x)=-x^{2}+ \text{constant} [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad v=y^{2}-x^{2}+ \text{constant}[/latex]

questions.question: a hemispherical furnace of 1m radius has the inner surface (emissivity, [latex]\varepsilon =1[/latex]  ) of its roof maintained at 800K, while its floor ([latex]\varepsilon =0.5[/latex] ) is kept at 600K. questions.explanation: Given data: [latex] \begin{aligned} r&=1 \mathrm{m} \\ \epsilon_{1} &=1 \\ T_{1} &=800 \mathrm{K} \\ \epsilon_{2} &=0.5 \\ T_{2} &=600 \mathrm{K} \\ \sigma &=5.668 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K}^{4} \\ \left(F_{9}\right)_{1-2} &=\frac{1}{\frac{1-\epsilon_{1}}{\epsilon_{1}}+\frac{1}{F_{12}}+\frac{A_{1}}{A_{2}}\left(\frac{1-\epsilon_{1}}{\epsilon_{2}}\right)} \\ F_{21} &=1 \\ A_{1} F_{12} &=A_{2} F_{21}\\ \Rightarrow \quad F_{12}&=\frac{A_{2}}{A_{1}}=\frac{\pi r^{2}}{2 \pi r^{2}}=\frac{1}{2} \\ \therefore \quad F&=\frac{1}{\left(\frac{1-1}{1}\right)+2+2\left(\frac{1-0.5}{0.5}\right)} \\ \quad=\frac{1}{4}&=0.25 \\ \therefore \quad Q_{1-2} &=\sigma A\left(F_{9}\right)_{1-2}\left[T_{1}^{4}-T_{2}^{4}\right] \\ Q_{12} &=5.668 \times 2 \times \pi \times(1)^{2} \\ & \times 0.25\left(800^{4}-600^{4}\right) \times 10^{-8} \\ Q_{12} &=24916.528 \mathrm{W}=24.916 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A material P of thickness 1 mm is sandwiched between two steel slabs, as shown in the figure below. A heat flux 10 [latex]kW/m^{2}[/latex] is supplied to one of the steel slabs as shown. The boundary temperatures of the slabs are indicated in the figure. Assume thermal conductivity of this steel is 10 W/m.K. Considering one-dimensional steady state heat conduction for the configuration, the thermal conductivity (k, in W/m.K) of material P is _______
questions.explanation: Given data: [latex] \begin{aligned} x &=1 \mathrm{mm}=0.001 \mathrm{m} \\ \mathrm{q}^{\prime \prime} &=10 \mathrm{kW} / \mathrm{m}^{2}=10000 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ k_{s} &=10 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} \\ \delta &=20 \mathrm{mm}=0.02 \mathrm{m} \\ T_{1} &=500 \mathrm{K} \\ T_{2} &=360 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex] [latex] \begin{aligned} \text { Heat flow: } Q&=\frac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{\frac{\delta}{k_{\mathrm{s}} A}+\frac{x}{k A}+\frac{\delta}{k_{\mathrm{s}} A}} \\ Q &=\frac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{\frac{2 \delta}{k_{s} A}+\frac{x}{k A}} \\ \frac{Q}{A}&= \frac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{\frac{2 \delta}{k_{s}}+\frac{x}{k}} \\ q^{\prime \prime}&=\frac{\frac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{2 \delta}+\frac{x}{k}}{k_{s}} \\ or q^{\prime \prime}\left(\frac{2 \delta}{k_{s}}+\frac{x}{k}\right)&=T_{1}-T_{2} \\ 10000\left(\frac{2 \times 0.02}{10}+\frac{0.001}{k}\right)&=500-360 \\ 40+\frac{10}{k}&=140 \\ or \quad \frac{10}{k}&=140-40=100 \\ or \quad k=\frac{10}{100}&=0.1 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: Consider laminar flow of water over a flat plate of length 1 m. If the  boundary layer thickness at a distance of 0.25 m from the leading edge of the plate is 8 mm, the boundary layer thickness  (in mm), at a distance of 0.75 m, is ______

questions.question: In an ideal Brayton cycle, atmospheric air (ratio of specific heats, [latex]c_{p}/c_{v} = 1.4[/latex] , specific heat at constant pressure = 1.005 kJ/kg.K) at 1 bar and 300 K is compressed to 8 bar. The maximum temperature in the cycle is limited to 1280 K. If the heat is supplied at the rate of 80 MW, the mass flow rate (in kg/s) of air required in the cycle is _______
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Given, } \frac{c_{p}}{c_{v}}&=\gamma=1.4 \\ c_{p} &=1.005 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ p_{1} &=1 \mathrm{bar} \\ T_{1} &=300 \mathrm{K} \\ p_{2} &=8 \mathrm{bar} \\ T_{3} &=T_{\max }=1280 \mathrm{K} \\ Q_{s} &=80 \mathrm{MW}=80 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}[/latex] For process 1-2 [latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}&=\left(\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\right)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}}=8^{\frac{0.4}{1.4}}=1.8114\\ \text{or}\quad T_{2} &=300 \times 1.8114=543.43 \mathrm{K} \\ Q_{s} &=m c_{p}\left(T_{3}-T_{2}\right) \\ 80 \times 10^{3} &=m \times 1.005(1280-543.43)\\ \text{or}\quad m&=108.07 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: In a concentric counter flow heat exchanger, water flows through the inner tube at 25[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and leaves at 42[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. The engine oil enters at 100[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and flows in the annular flow passage. The exit temperature of the engine oil is 50[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. Mass flow rate of water and the engine oil are 1.5 kg/s and 1 kg/s, respectively. The specific heat of water and oil are 4178 J/kg.K and 2130 J/kg.K, respectively. The effectiveness of this heat exchanger is _______
questions.explanation: Given data: [latex] \begin{aligned} c_{c}=4178 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} ; c_{h}&=2130 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ m_{c}=1.5 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; m_{h}&=1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ C_{\min }=& c_{h} m_{h}=2130 \times 1=2130 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{k} \\ C_{\max }=& c_{c} m_{c}=4178 \times 1.5 \\ =& 6267 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{K} \\ \Delta T_{1}=& 100-42=58^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{2}=& 50-25=25^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{l m} =&\frac{\Delta T_{1}-\Delta T_{2}}{\ln \left(\frac{\Delta T_{1}}{\Delta T_{2}}\right)} \\ =& \ln \left(\frac{58}{25}\right)=39.21^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ Q=& \mathrm{UA} \Delta T_{\mathrm{Im}} \\ \text{ also}\quad Q=& m_{c} c_{\mathrm{c}}\left(T_{\mathrm{c} 2}-T_{\mathrm{c} 1}\right) \\ \therefore \quad UA \Delta T_{l m}=&m_{c} c_{c}\left(T_{c 2}-T_{c 1}\right) \\ U A =&\frac{4178 \times 1.5(42-25)}{39.21} \\ =&2717.138 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex] [latex]\begin{aligned} \mathrm{NTU} &=\frac{\mathrm{UA}}{\mathrm{C}_{\min }}=\frac{2717}{2130}=1.2756 \\ C &=\frac{C_{\min }}{C_{\max }}=\frac{2130}{6267}=0.34 \\ &=\frac{1-\exp [-N T U(1-C)]}{1-C \exp [-N T U(1-C)]} \\ &=\frac{1-\exp [-1.2756 \times 0.66]}{1-0.34 \exp [1-2756 \times 0.66]} \\ &=\frac{1-0.43}{1-0.34 \times 0.43}=0.6676\\ Alternatively:\\ \epsilon &=\frac{T_{h_{1}}-T_{h_{2}}}{T_{h_{1}}-T_{c_{1}}} \\ &=\frac{100-50}{100-25} \\ &=\frac{50}{75}=\frac{2}{3}=0.6667 \end{aligned}[/latex]

Given data:
[latex] \begin{aligned} c_{c}=4178 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} ; c_{h}&=2130 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ m_{c}=1.5 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; m_{h}&=1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ C_{\min }=& c_{h} m_{h}=2130 \times 1=2130 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{k} \\ C_{\max }=& c_{c} m_{c}=4178 \times 1.5 \\ =& 6267 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{K} \\ \Delta T_{1}=& 100-42=58^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{2}=& 50-25=25^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{l m} =&\frac{\Delta T_{1}-\Delta T_{2}}{\ln \left(\frac{\Delta T_{1}}{\Delta T_{2}}\right)} \\ =& \ln \left(\frac{58}{25}\right)=39.21^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ Q=& \mathrm{UA} \Delta T_{\mathrm{Im}} \\ \text{ also}\quad Q=& m_{c} c_{\mathrm{c}}\left(T_{\mathrm{c} 2}-T_{\mathrm{c} 1}\right) \\ \therefore \quad UA \Delta T_{l m}=&m_{c} c_{c}\left(T_{c 2}-T_{c 1}\right) \\ U A =&\frac{4178 \times 1.5(42-25)}{39.21} \\ =&2717.138 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A heat pump with refrigerant R22 is used for space heating between temperature limits of -20[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and 25[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. The heat required is 200 MJ/h. Assume specific heat of vapour at the time of discharge as 0.98 kJ/kg.K. Other relevant properties are given below. questions.question: A project has four activities P, Q, R and S as shown below. The normal cost of the project is Rs. 10,000 and the overhead cost is Rs. 200 per day. If the project duration has to be crashed down to 9 days, the total cost (in Rupees) of the project is _______
questions.explanation: Path P-Q = 10 days P-R-S = 3+4+5 = 12 days So P-R-S is critical path Now we will crash the activity 'S' by 2 day So now P-R = 10 day P-R-S = 10 day both are critical paths So Total cost of project will be = Normal cost + overhead cost + crashing cost = 10000+200*(10 day) +200*2 = 10000+2000+400 = 12400 Rs

[latex] \therefore \quad \frac{\sigma_{m}}{\sigma_{y}}+\frac{\sigma_{a}}{\sigma_{e}}=\frac{1}{N}[/latex] [latex] \text{or }\quad 0+\frac{100}{200}=\frac{1}{N} \Rightarrow N=2[/latex]

Relative humidity

Absolute humidity,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \omega &=\frac{0.622 p_{v}}{p-p_{v}} \\ &=\frac{0.622 \times 2.756}{85-2.756} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: An analytic function of a complex variable [latex]z=x+iy[/latex]  is expressed as [latex]f(z)=u(x,y)+iv(x,y)[/latex]  , where [latex]i=\sqrt{-1}[/latex]. If [latex]u(x,y)=x^{2}-y^{2}[/latex], then expression for [latex]v(x,y)[/latex]  in terms of x, y and a general constant c would be
questions.explanation: As per Cauchy-Riemann equations: [latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} and \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} [/latex] [latex] u=x^{2}-y^{2} [/latex] [latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=2 x, \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-2 y [/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 x [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad v=2 x y+f(x) [/latex] [latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 y+f(x) [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 y+f^{\prime}(x) [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=0 \quad \text { i.e. } f(x)=c [/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad v=2 x y+c [/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
As per Cauchy-Riemann equations:
[latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} and \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} [/latex]
[latex] u=x^{2}-y^{2} [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=2 x, \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-2 y [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 x [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad v=2 x y+f(x) [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 y+f(x) [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 y+f^{\prime}(x) [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=0 \quad \text { i.e. } f(x)=c [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad v=2 x y+c [/latex]

questions.question: Consider two solutions [latex]x(t)=x_{1}(t)[/latex] and  [latex]x(t)=x_{2}(t)[/latex]  of the differential equation [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d}^2x(t)}{\mathrm{d} t^{2}}+x(t)=0,\; t\gt 0[/latex]  , such that [latex]x_{1}(0)=1,\; \frac{\mathrm{d}x_{1}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t}|_{t=0} =0,x_{2}(0)=0,\frac{\mathrm{d}x_{2}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t}|_{t=0} =1[/latex]  . The wronskian [latex]W(t)=\begin{vmatrix} x_{1}(t) & x_{2}(t)\\ \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{1}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t} & \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{2}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t} \end{vmatrix}[/latex]  at [latex]t=\pi /2[/latex]  is.
questions.explanation: Given differential equation in symbolic form is [latex] \left(D^{2}+1\right) x(t)=0 [/latex] Its A.E. is [latex] D^{2}+1=0 [/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad D=\pm i [/latex] So, C.F. is [latex] x_{1}(t)=C_{1} \cos t [/latex] [latex] x_{2}(t)=C_{2} \sin t[/latex] [latex] \therefore x_{1}(0)=C_{1}=1 [/latex] [latex] \begin{array}{l} \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad x_{1}(t) &=\operatorname{cost} \\ \text { it satisfies }\left.\begin{matrix} \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{1}(t)}{d t}\end{matrix} \right|_{t=0} &=0 \end{aligned} \\ \qquad \begin{aligned} x_{2}(0) &=0=C_{2} \sin (0)\left(\because C_{2} \neq 0\right) \\ \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t} &=C_{2} \cos t \end{aligned} \\ \left.\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t}\right|_{t=0}=C_{2}=1 \end{array}[/latex] [latex] \begin{array}{l} \therefore  \;\; x_{2}(t)=\sin t \\ W(t)= \begin{vmatrix} x_{1}(t) & x_{2}(t) \\ \frac{d x_{1}(t)}{d t} & \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t}\end{vmatrix}= \begin{vmatrix} \cos t & \sin t \\ -\sin t & \cos t \end{vmatrix} \\ M(t)=\cos ^{2} t+\sin ^{2} t=1 \end{array}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given differential equation in symbolic form is
[latex] \left(D^{2}+1\right) x(t)=0 [/latex]
Its A.E. is [latex] D^{2}+1=0 [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad D=\pm i [/latex]
So, C.F. is
[latex] x_{1}(t)=C_{1} \cos t [/latex]
[latex] x_{2}(t)=C_{2} \sin t[/latex]
[latex] \therefore x_{1}(0)=C_{1}=1 [/latex]
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad x_{1}(t) &=\operatorname{cost} \\ \text { it satisfies }\left.\begin{matrix} \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{1}(t)}{d t}\end{matrix} \right|_{t=0} &=0 \end{aligned} \\ \qquad \begin{aligned} x_{2}(0) &=0=C_{2} \sin (0)\left(\because C_{2} \neq 0\right) \\ \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t} &=C_{2} \cos t \end{aligned} \\ \left.\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t}\right|_{t=0}=C_{2}=1 \end{array}[/latex]
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \therefore \;\; x_{2}(t)=\sin t \\ W(t)= \begin{vmatrix} x_{1}(t) & x_{2}(t) \\ \frac{d x_{1}(t)}{d t} & \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t}\end{vmatrix}= \begin{vmatrix} \cos t & \sin t \\ -\sin t & \cos t \end{vmatrix} \\ M(t)=\cos ^{2} t+\sin ^{2} t=1 \end{array}[/latex]

questions.question: A machine produces 0, 1 or 2 defective pieces in a day with associated probability of 1/6, 2/3 and 1/6, respectively. The mean value and the variance of the number of defective pieces produced by the machine in a day,  respectively, are

questions.question: A four-wheel vehicle of mass 1000 kg moves uniformly in a straight line with the wheels revolving at 10 rad/s. The wheels are identical, each with a radius of 0.2 m. Then a constant braking torque is applied to all the wheels and the vehicle experiences a uniform deceleration. For the vehicle to stop in 10 s, the braking torque (in N.m) on each wheel is _______
questions.explanation: Initial velocity, [latex] u=\omega r=10 \times 0.2=2 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}[/latex] For vehicle to stop, [latex] \begin{aligned} v &=u-\mathrm{at} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0 &=u-\mathrm{at}\\ \therefore \quad a&=\frac{u}{t}=\frac{2}{10}=0.2 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex] Braking force = Total mass x deceleration [latex] \begin{aligned} F &=1000 \times 0.2 \\ &=200 \mathrm{N} \\ F_{\text {each wheel }} &=\frac{200}{4}=50 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}[/latex] Braking torque on each wheel [latex] =50 \times 0.2=10 \mathrm{Nm}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Initial velocity,
[latex] u=\omega r=10 \times 0.2=2 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}[/latex]
For vehicle to stop,
[latex] \begin{aligned} v &=u-\mathrm{at} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0 &=u-\mathrm{at}\\ \therefore \quad a&=\frac{u}{t}=\frac{2}{10}=0.2 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Braking force = Total mass x deceleration
[latex] \begin{aligned} F &=1000 \times 0.2 \\ &=200 \mathrm{N} \\ F_{\text {each wheel }} &=\frac{200}{4}=50 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Braking torque on each wheel
[latex] =50 \times 0.2=10 \mathrm{Nm}[/latex]

questions.question: Consider an objective function [latex]Z(x_{1},x_{2})=3x_{1}+9x_{2}[/latex] and the constraints [latex]x_{1}+x_{2}\leq 8,[/latex] [latex] x_{1}+2x_{2}\leq 4, [/latex] [latex] x_{1}\geq 0,x_{2}\geq 0.[/latex] The maximum value of the objective function is __________
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} (Z)_{(4,0)}&=3 \times 4+9 \times 0=12 \\ (Z)_{(0,2)}&=3 \times 0+9 \times 2=18 \\ (Z)_{(0,0)}&=0 \quad \text { (Trivial solution) } \\ Z_{\max }&=18 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A mass-spring-dashpot system with mass m = 10 kg, spring constant k = 6250 N/m is excited by a harmonic excitation of [latex]10 cos(25t)[/latex] N. At the steady state, the vibration amplitude of the mass is   40 mm. The damping coefficient (c, in N.s/m) of the dashpot is _______
questions.explanation:
[latex]\begin{array}{l} \text { Given, } m=10 \mathrm{kg}, F_{0}=10 \mathrm{N} \\ \omega=25 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}, k=6250 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m} \\ X =\frac{F_{0}}{\sqrt{\left(k-m \omega^{2}\right)^{2}+(c \omega)^{2}}}\\ \text{or}\quad \sqrt{\left(k-m \omega^{2}\right)^{2}+(c \omega)^{2}}=\frac{F_{0}}{X} \\ \end{array}[/latex] [latex] \begin{aligned} (c \omega) &=\sqrt{\left(\frac{F_{0}}{X}\right)^{2}-\left(k-m \omega^{2}\right)^{2}} \\ &=\sqrt{\left(\frac{10}{0.04}\right)^{2}-(6250-10 \times 625)^{2}}\\c \omega &=\frac{10}{0.04}=250 \\
\therefore \quad c &=\frac{250}{\omega}=\frac{250}{25}=10 \mathrm{Ns} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned} [/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{array}{l} \text { Given, } m=10 \mathrm{kg}, F_{0}=10 \mathrm{N} \\ \omega=25 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}, k=6250 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m} \\ X =\frac{F_{0}}{\sqrt{\left(k-m \omega^{2}\right)^{2}+(c \omega)^{2}}}\\ \text{or}\quad \sqrt{\left(k-m \omega^{2}\right)^{2}+(c \omega)^{2}}=\frac{F_{0}}{X} \\ \end{array}[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} (c \omega) &=\sqrt{\left(\frac{F_{0}}{X}\right)^{2}-\left(k-m \omega^{2}\right)^{2}} \\ &=\sqrt{\left(\frac{10}{0.04}\right)^{2}-(6250-10 \times 625)^{2}}\\c \omega &=\frac{10}{0.04}=250 \\ \therefore \quad c &=\frac{250}{\omega}=\frac{250}{25}=10 \mathrm{Ns} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned} [/latex]

questions.question: A certain amount of an ideal gas is initially at a pressure [latex]p_{1}[/latex]  and temperature [latex]T_{1}[/latex] . First, it undergoes a constant pressure process 1-2 such that [latex]T_{2}[/latex]=[latex]3T_{1}/4[/latex]. Then, it undergoes a constant volume process  2-3 such that [latex]T_{3}[/latex]=[latex]T_{1}/2[/latex]. The ratio of the final volume to the initial volume of the ideal gas is
questions.explanation: Process 1-2: Cooling at p=C [latex] T=\frac{3 T_{1}}{4} \text { given condition }[/latex] [latex] \text{Or} \quad \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}=\frac{3}{4}[/latex] According to Charle's law [latex] \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}=\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}=\frac{3}{4}[/latex] Process 2-3: Cooling at V=C [latex] \begin{aligned} T_{3} &=\frac{T_{2}}{2} \text { given condition } \\ \frac{\text { Final volume }}{\text { Initial volume }} &=\frac{V_{3}}{V_{1}}=\frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}} \quad \because V_{3}=V_{2} \\ &=\frac{3}{4}=0.75 \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Process 1-2: Cooling at p=C
[latex] T=\frac{3 T_{1}}{4} \text { given condition }[/latex]
[latex] \text{Or} \quad \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}=\frac{3}{4}[/latex]
According to Charle's law
[latex] \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}=\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}=\frac{3}{4}[/latex]
Process 2-3: Cooling at V=C
[latex] \begin{aligned} T_{3} &=\frac{T_{2}}{2} \text { given condition } \\ \frac{\text { Final volume }}{\text { Initial volume }} &=\frac{V_{3}}{V_{1}}=\frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}} \quad \because V_{3}=V_{2} \\ &=\frac{3}{4}=0.75 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: Heat transfer through a composite wall is shown in figure. Both the sections of the wall have equal thickness ([latex]l[/latex]). The conductivity of one section is k and that of the other is 2k. The left face of the wall is at 600 K and the right face is at 300 K. The interface temperature [latex]T_{i}[/latex] (in K) of the composite wall is  _______
questions.explanation: Given data: [latex] \begin{aligned} T_{1}&=600 \mathrm{K} \\ T_{2}&=300 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex] For steady state heat transfer, Heat flow through layer-1 = Heat flow through layer-2 [latex] \begin{aligned} Q&=Q \\ \frac{T_{1}-T_{i}}{l / k A}&=\frac{T_{i}-T_{2}}{l / 2 k A} \\ \frac{k A\left(T_{1}-T_{i}\right)}{l}&=\frac{2 k A\left(T_{i}-T_{2}\right)}{l}\\ \text{or }\quad T_{1}-T_{i}&=2 T_{i}-2 T_{2} \\ \text{or }\quad T_{1}+2 T_{2}&=3 T_{i} \\ \text{or }\quad T_{i} &=\frac{T_{1}+2 T_{2}}{3} \\ &=\frac{600+2 \times 300}{3}=400^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given data:
[latex] \begin{aligned} T_{1}&=600 \mathrm{K} \\ T_{2}&=300 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]


For steady state heat transfer,
Heat flow through layer-1
= Heat flow through layer-2
[latex] \begin{aligned} Q&=Q \\ \frac{T_{1}-T_{i}}{l / k A}&=\frac{T_{i}-T_{2}}{l / 2 k A} \\ \frac{k A\left(T_{1}-T_{i}\right)}{l}&=\frac{2 k A\left(T_{i}-T_{2}\right)}{l}\\ \text{or }\quad T_{1}-T_{i}&=2 T_{i}-2 T_{2} \\ \text{or }\quad T_{1}+2 T_{2}&=3 T_{i} \\ \text{or }\quad T_{i} &=\frac{T_{1}+2 T_{2}}{3} \\ &=\frac{600+2 \times 300}{3}=400^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A fluid of dynamic viscosity [latex]2\times 10^{-5}[/latex] kg/m.s and density 1 [latex]kg/m^{3}[/latex] flows with an average velocity of 1 m/s through a long duct of rectangular (25 mm x 15 mm) cross-section. Assuming laminar flow, the pressure drop (in Pa) in the fully developed region per meter length of the duct is _______
questions.explanation: Given data: [latex] \begin{aligned} \mu&=2 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{ms} \\ \rho&=1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \bar{u}&=1 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex] [latex] a=25 \mathrm{mm}=0.025 \mathrm{m} [/latex] [latex] b=15 \mathrm{mm}=0.015 \mathrm{m} [/latex] Characteristic diameter, [latex] D_{c}=\frac{4 A}{P}[/latex] where [latex] \qquad A=a \times b,[/latex] cross-section area [latex] =0.025 \times 0.015 [/latex] [latex] =3.75 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{m}^{2}[/latex] and [latex] \qquad \mathrm{P}=2(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}),[/latex] wetted perimeter [latex] =2(0.025+0.015)=0.08 \mathrm{m}[/latex] [latex] \therefore \qquad D_{c}=\frac{4 \times 3.74 \times 10^{-4}}{0.08}=0.0187 \mathrm{m}[/latex] Pressure drop, [latex] \begin{aligned} \Delta p &=\frac{32 \mu \bar{u} L}{D_{c}^{2}} \\ \frac{\Delta p}{L} &=\frac{32 \mu \bar{u}}{D_{c}^{2}} \\ &=\frac{32 \times 2 \times 10^{-5} \times 1}{(0.0187)^{2}} \\ &=1.83 \mathrm{Pa} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

Given data:
[latex] \begin{aligned} \mu&=2 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{ms} \\ \rho&=1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \bar{u}&=1 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex] \therefore \qquad D_{c}=\frac{4 \times 3.74 \times 10^{-4}}{0.08}=0.0187 \mathrm{m}[/latex]

questions.question: At the inlet of an axial impulse turbine rotor, the blade linear speed is 25 m/s, the magnitude of absolute velocity is 100 m/s and the angle between them is 25[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]. The relative velocity and the axial component of velocity remain the same between the inlet and outlet of the blades. The blade inlet and outlet velocity triangles are shown in the figure. Assuming no losses, the specific work (in J/kg) is _______
questions.explanation: Given data: [latex] \begin{aligned} u &=25 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V_{i} &=100 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \alpha_{i} &=25^{\circ} \\ V_{r_{i}}=V_{r_{0}} &=78 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V_{0} &=58.6 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V_{t_{i}} &=V_{r_{U}} \end{aligned}[/latex] [latex] \begin{aligned} \cos \alpha_{i} &=\frac{V_{w i}}{V_{i}} \\ \cos 25^{\circ} &=\frac{V_{w i}}{100} \\ or \quad V_{w_{i}}&=100 \times \cos 25^{\circ}=90.36 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}\\ \sin \alpha_{i} &=\frac{V_{f_{i}}}{V_{i}} \\ \sin 25^{\circ} &=\frac{V_{f_{i}}}{100} \\ or \quad V_{f_{i}}&=100 \times \sin 25^{\circ}=42.26 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V_{w_{0}} &=\sqrt{V_{0}^{2}-V_{f_{0}}^{2}} \\ &=\sqrt{(58.6)^{2}-(42.26)^{2}}=40.59 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \text{Specific work,}\\ w&=\left(V_{w_{i}}+V_{w_{0}}\right) u \\ &=(90.63+40.59) \times 25 \\ &=3280.5 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kg} \\ \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A double -price counter-flow heat exchanger transfers heat between two water streams. Tube side water at 19 liters/s is heated from 10[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C to 38[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. Shell side, water at 25 liters/s is entering at 46[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. Assume constant properties of water, destiny is 1000kg/[latex]m^{3}[/latex] and specific heat is 4186 J/kg.K. The LMTD (in [latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C) is ________
questions.explanation: Given data: [latex] T_{h 1}=46^{\circ} \mathrm{C} ; \quad T_{n 2}=? ; \quad T_{c 1}=10^{\circ} \mathrm{C} ; \quad T_{c 2}=38^{\circ} \mathrm{C} [/latex] [latex] \rho_{\text {water }}=1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} [/latex] [latex] m_{c}=19 \mathrm{L} / \mathrm{s}, m_{n}=25 \mathrm{L} / \mathrm{s} [/latex] From energy balance, [latex] \begin{aligned} m_{c} c_{c}\left(T_{c 2}-T_{c 1}\right)&=m_{h} c_{h}\left(T_{h 1}-T_{h 2}\right) \\ 19 \times(38-10) &=25\left(46-T_{h_{2}}\right) \\ \text { or } \quad T_{h_{2}} &=46-\frac{19 \times 28}{25}=24.72^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{1} &=T_{h_{1}}-T_{c_{2}}=46-38=8^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{2} &=T_{h_{2}}-T_{G}=24.72-10 \\ &=14.72^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \mathrm{LMTD} &=\frac{\Delta T_{1}-\Delta T_{2}}{\ln \left(\frac{\Delta T_{1}}{\Delta T_{2}}\right)} \\ &=\frac{8-14.72}{\ln \left(\frac{8}{14.72}\right)}=\frac{6.72}{0.60976} \\ &=11.02^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given data:
[latex] T_{h 1}=46^{\circ} \mathrm{C} ; \quad T_{n 2}=? ; \quad T_{c 1}=10^{\circ} \mathrm{C} ; \quad T_{c 2}=38^{\circ} \mathrm{C} [/latex]
[latex] \rho_{\text {water }}=1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} [/latex]
[latex] m_{c}=19 \mathrm{L} / \mathrm{s}, m_{n}=25 \mathrm{L} / \mathrm{s} [/latex]
From energy balance,
[latex] \begin{aligned} m_{c} c_{c}\left(T_{c 2}-T_{c 1}\right)&=m_{h} c_{h}\left(T_{h 1}-T_{h 2}\right) \\ 19 \times(38-10) &=25\left(46-T_{h_{2}}\right) \\ \text { or } \quad T_{h_{2}} &=46-\frac{19 \times 28}{25}=24.72^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{1} &=T_{h_{1}}-T_{c_{2}}=46-38=8^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{2} &=T_{h_{2}}-T_{G}=24.72-10 \\ &=14.72^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \mathrm{LMTD} &=\frac{\Delta T_{1}-\Delta T_{2}}{\ln \left(\frac{\Delta T_{1}}{\Delta T_{2}}\right)} \\ &=\frac{8-14.72}{\ln \left(\frac{8}{14.72}\right)}=\frac{6.72}{0.60976} \\ &=11.02^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A diesel engine has a compression ratio of 17 and cut-off takes place at 10% of the stroke. Assuming ratio of specific heats ([latex]\gamma[/latex]) as 1.4, the air-standard effeciency is _________
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}&=17 \\ \frac{c_{p}}{c_{v}}&=\gamma=1.4 \\ \text { or } \quad V_{3}-V_{2}&=0.1\left(V_{1}-V_{2}\right) \\ \text { or } \quad \frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}-1&=0.1\left(\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}-1\right)\\ \text { or } \quad \frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}&=0.1 \times 16+1=2.6\\ r_{c}&=\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}=2.6\\ &\begin{array}{l} \eta_{\text {Disel }}=1-\frac{1}{r^{\gamma-1}}\left[\frac{r_{c}^{\gamma}-1}{\gamma\left(r_{c}-1\right)}\right] \\ \begin{array}{l} =1-\frac{1}{17^{0.4}}\left[\frac{2.6^{1.4}-1}{1.4(2.6-1)}\right] \\ =1-\frac{1}{17^{0.4}}\left(\frac{3.81-1}{1.4 \times 1.6}\right)\\=0.596=59.6 \% \end{array} \end{array} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}&=17 \\ \frac{c_{p}}{c_{v}}&=\gamma=1.4 \\ \text { or } \quad V_{3}-V_{2}&=0.1\left(V_{1}-V_{2}\right) \\ \text { or } \quad \frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}-1&=0.1\left(\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}-1\right)\\ \text { or } \quad \frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}&=0.1 \times 16+1=2.6\\ r_{c}&=\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}=2.6\\ &\begin{array}{l} \eta_{\text {Disel }}=1-\frac{1}{r^{\gamma-1}}\left[\frac{r_{c}^{\gamma}-1}{\gamma\left(r_{c}-1\right)}\right] \\ \begin{array}{l} =1-\frac{1}{17^{0.4}}\left[\frac{2.6^{1.4}-1}{1.4(2.6-1)}\right] \\ =1-\frac{1}{17^{0.4}}\left(\frac{3.81-1}{1.4 \times 1.6}\right)\\=0.596=59.6 \% \end{array} \end{array} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: The diameter of a recessed ring was measured by using two spherical balls of diameter [latex]d_{2}=60[/latex]  mm and [latex]d_{1}=40[/latex]  mm as shown in the figure. The distance [latex]H_{2}=35.55[/latex]  mm and [latex]H_{1}=20.55[/latex]  mm. The diameter (D, in mm) of the ring gauge  is _______
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} d_1 &=60mm \\ d_2&= 40mm\\ \frac{d_1}{2}&=30mm \\ \frac{d_2}{2}&=20mm \\ H_1&= 35.55mm\\ H_2&=20.55mm \\ D&= \frac{d_1}{2}+AB+\frac{d_2}{2}\\ BC&=\left ( H_1+\frac{d_1}{2} \right )-\left ( H_2+\frac{d_2}{2} \right ) \\ &=(35.55+30)-(20.55+20) \\ &=65.55-40.55=25mm \\ &\text{In right angle } \; \Delta ABC \\ AC&= \frac{d_1}{2}+\frac{d_2}{2}\\ &= 30+20=50mm\\ AB&=\sqrt{AC^2-BC^2} \\ &= \sqrt{50^2-25^2}=25\sqrt{3}mm\\ D&=30+25\sqrt{3}+20=93.30mm \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: Which pair of following statements is correct for orthogonal cutting using a single-point cutting tool? P.  Reduction in friction angle increases cutting force Q. Reduction in friction angle decreases cutting force R. Reduction in friction angle increases chip thickness S. Reduction in friction angle decreases chip thickness
questions.explanation: For orthogonal cutting using a single-point cutting tool reduction in friction angle will increase the shear angle From Merchant theory [latex]\phi =\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\alpha }{2}-\frac{\beta }{2}[/latex] [latex]\alpha \rightarrow[/latex] rate angle (constant) [latex]\beta \rightarrow[/latex] friction angle [latex]\phi \rightarrow[/latex] shear angle [latex]\beta \downarrow \phi \uparrow[/latex] we can see that as shear angle will increase shear plane area will get decrease which results decrease in cutting force subsequently reduction in chip thickness.
questions.explanation_html:
For orthogonal cutting using a single-point cutting tool reduction in friction angle will increase the shear angle
From Merchant theory
[latex]\phi =\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\alpha }{2}-\frac{\beta }{2}[/latex]
[latex]\alpha \rightarrow[/latex] rate angle (constant)
[latex]\beta \rightarrow[/latex] friction angle
[latex]\phi \rightarrow[/latex] shear angle
[latex]\beta \downarrow \phi \uparrow[/latex]

we can see that as shear angle will increase shear plane area will get decrease which results decrease in cutting force subsequently reduction in chip thickness.

Total heat generation
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=I^{2} R t \\ &=(10000)^{2} \times 0.0002 \times 0.2 \\ &=4000 \mathrm{J} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Heat required to melt the nugget

questions.question: The value of the integral [latex]\int_{0}^{2}\frac{(x-1)^{2}\sin(x-1)}{(x-1)^{2}+\cos(x-1)}dx[/latex] is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} I &= \int_{0}^{2}\frac{(x-1)^2 \sin (x-1)}{(x-1)^2 + \cos (x-1)}dx\\ \text{Taking}\; x-1=z&\Rightarrow dx=dz \\ \text{for}\; x=0,&z\rightarrow -1\; \text{and}\; x=2, z \rightarrow 1 \\ \therefore \; I &=\int_{-1}^{1} \frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+\cos z}dz\\ \text{let}\;\; f(z)&=\frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+ \cos z} dz\\ f(-z) &= \frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+ \cos z}\\ f(z)&= -f(z) \; \text{function is ODD}\\ \therefore \;\; I&=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} I &= \int_{0}^{2}\frac{(x-1)^2 \sin (x-1)}{(x-1)^2 + \cos (x-1)}dx\\ \text{Taking}\; x-1=z&\Rightarrow dx=dz \\ \text{for}\; x=0,&z\rightarrow -1\; \text{and}\; x=2, z \rightarrow 1 \\ \therefore \; I &=\int_{-1}^{1} \frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+\cos z}dz\\ \text{let}\;\; f(z)&=\frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+ \cos z} dz\\ f(-z) &= \frac{z^2 \sin z}{z^2+ \cos z}\\ f(z)&= -f(z) \; \text{function is ODD}\\ \therefore \;\; I&=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A reversed Carnot cycle refrigerator maintains a temperature of -5[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. The ambient air temperature is 35[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. questions.explanation_html:
Given data:
[latex] \begin{array}{l} T_{2}=-5^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=(-5+273) \mathrm{K}=268 \mathrm{K} \\ T_{1}=35^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=(35+273) \mathrm{K}=308 \mathrm{K} \end{array}[/latex]


[latex] \begin{aligned} Q_{2}=2.5 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{s}&=2.5 \mathrm{kW}=2500 \mathrm{W} \\ (\mathrm{COP})_{R} &=\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}-T_{2}} \\ &=\frac{268}{308-268}=6.7 \\ \text { also } \quad(\mathrm{COP})_{R} &=\frac{Q_{2}}{W}\\ \therefore \quad 6.7&=\frac{2500}{W}\\ \text{or }\quad W&=\frac{2500}{6.7}=373.13 \text { watt } \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: The number of accidents occurring in a plant in a month follows Poisson distribution with mean as 5.2. The probability of occurrence of less than 2 accidents in the plant during a randomly selected month is
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} P(x) &=\frac{\mu^{x} \mathrm{e}^{-\mu}}{x !} \\ P(x \lt 2) &=P(0)+P(1) \\ &=\frac{\mu^{0} e^{-\mu}}{0 !}+\frac{\mu^{1} e^{-\mu}}{1 !} \\ &=\frac{1}{e^{\mu}}+\frac{\mu}{e^{\mu}}=\frac{1+\mu}{e^{\mu}} \\ \operatorname{As} \mu(\operatorname{mean})=5 & \cdot 2 \\ \therefore \quad P(x \lt 2) &=\frac{6.2}{e^{5.2}}=0.0342 \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} P(x) &=\frac{\mu^{x} \mathrm{e}^{-\mu}}{x !} \\ P(x \lt 2) &=P(0)+P(1) \\ &=\frac{\mu^{0} e^{-\mu}}{0 !}+\frac{\mu^{1} e^{-\mu}}{1 !} \\ &=\frac{1}{e^{\mu}}+\frac{\mu}{e^{\mu}}=\frac{1+\mu}{e^{\mu}} \\ \operatorname{As} \mu(\operatorname{mean})=5 & \cdot 2 \\ \therefore \quad P(x \lt 2) &=\frac{6.2}{e^{5.2}}=0.0342 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.explanation: [latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{d x}{d t} &=4 t+4 \\ &=f\left(t_{0}, x_{0}\right) \\ \text { At } t=0, & x=x_{0} \end{aligned} [/latex] Irrespective of values of [latex] x, f\left(t_{0}, x_{0}\right)[/latex] depends on t only. [latex] \begin{aligned} k_{1} &=h f\left(t_{0}, x_{0}\right)=0.2 x \times 4=0.8 \\ \mathrm{k}_{2} &=h f\left(t_{0}+\frac{1}{2} h, x_{0}+\frac{k_{1}}{2}\right) \\ &=h f\left(0.1, x_{0}+0.4\right) \\ &=0.2(4 \times 0.1+4)=0.88 \\ k_{3} &=h f\left(t_{0}+\frac{1}{2} h, x_{0}+\frac{k_{2}}{2}\right) \\ &=0.2 f\left(0.1, x_{0}+0.44\right) \\ &=0.2(4 \times 0.1+4)=0.88 \\ k_{4} &=h f\left(t_{0}+h, x_{0}+k_{3}\right) \\ &=0.2 f\left(0.2, x_{0}+0.88\right) \\ &=0.2(4 \times 0.2+4)=0.96 \\ k &=\frac{1}{6}\left(k_{1}+2 k_{2}+2 k_{3}+k_{4}\right) \\ &=\frac{1}{6}(0.8+2 \times 0.88+2 \times 0.88+0.96) \\ &=0.88 \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A shaft is subjected to pure torsional moment. The maximum shear stress developed in the shaft is 100 MPa. The yield and ultimate strengths of the shaft material in tension are 300 MPa and  450 MPa, respectively. The factor of safety using maximum distortion energy (von-Mises) theory  is  _______
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \sigma_{1}&=100 \mathrm{MPa} \\ \sigma_{2}&=-100 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}[/latex] As per Von-Mises yield theory: [latex] N^{2}\left[\left(\sigma_{1}-\sigma_{2}\right)^{2}+\left(\sigma_{2}-\sigma_{3}\right)^{2}+\left(\sigma_{1}-\sigma_{3}\right)^{2}\right] \leq 2 \sigma_{y}^{2} [/latex] [latex] \text{In this case,  } \sigma_{3}=0 [/latex] [latex] 2 N^{2}\left[\sigma_{1}^{2}+\sigma_{2}^{2}-\sigma_{1} \sigma_{2}\right] \leq 2 \sigma_{y}^{2} [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow N^{2}\left[(100)^{2}+(100)^{2}+(100)^{2}\right] \leq(300)^{2} [/latex] [latex] \Rightarrow N^{2}=\frac{9}{3} \Rightarrow N \leq \sqrt{3} [/latex] [latex] \therefore \quad N=1.732[/latex]
questions.topic: Static Dynamic Loading and Failure Theories
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \sigma_{1}&=100 \mathrm{MPa} \\ \sigma_{2}&=-100 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]
As per Von-Mises yield theory:


[latex] N^{2}\left[\left(\sigma_{1}-\sigma_{2}\right)^{2}+\left(\sigma_{2}-\sigma_{3}\right)^{2}+\left(\sigma_{1}-\sigma_{3}\right)^{2}\right] \leq 2 \sigma_{y}^{2} [/latex]
[latex] \text{In this case, } \sigma_{3}=0 [/latex]
[latex] 2 N^{2}\left[\sigma_{1}^{2}+\sigma_{2}^{2}-\sigma_{1} \sigma_{2}\right] \leq 2 \sigma_{y}^{2} [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow N^{2}\left[(100)^{2}+(100)^{2}+(100)^{2}\right] \leq(300)^{2} [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow N^{2}=\frac{9}{3} \Rightarrow N \leq \sqrt{3} [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad N=1.732[/latex]

questions.explanation: For [latex]20^{\circ}[/latex] stub pressure angle spur gears pair minimum number of teeth on the pinion can be expressed as [latex]t_{min}=\frac{2A_p}{\sqrt{1+G(G+2)\sin ^2 \phi -1}}[/latex] Where, [latex]A_p:[/latex] Fractional addendum for one module in order to avoid interference. [latex]G:[/latex] Gear ration [latex]\phi :[/latex] Pressure angle Now we have given that speed ratio is increased & we know that; [latex]\text{Speed ratio}=\frac{1}{\text{gear ratio}}[/latex] So if gear ratio is increased we can say that minimum number of teeth on pinion must be increase to avoid interference.

questions.question: A uniform slender rod (8 m length and 3 kg mass) rotates in a vertical plane about a horizontal axis 1 m from its end as shown in the figure. The magnitude of the angular acceleration (in rad/[latex]s^{2}[/latex]) of the rod at the position shown is  _______
questions.explanation: [latex] \begin{aligned} A P &=1 \mathrm{m} \\ A C &=4 \mathrm{m} \\ P C &=3 \mathrm{m} \\ I_{C} &=\frac{m L^{2}}{12}=\frac{3 \times 8 \times 8}{12} \\ &=16 \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{m}^{2} \\ I_{P} &=I_{C}+m(P C)^{2} \\ &=16+3 \times 3^{2}=43 \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \text { Torque } &=m_{2} g \times \frac{P B}{2}-m_{1} g \frac{A P}{2} \\ T &=m_{2} \times 9.81 \times \frac{7}{2}-m_{1} \times 9.81 \times \frac{1}{2}\\ &=34.335 \mathrm{m}_{2}-4.905 \mathrm{m}_{1} \\ m_{1} &=\frac{3}{8} \mathrm{kg}, \mathrm{m}_{2}=\frac{3 \times 7}{8}=2.625 \\ T &=34.335 \times 2.625-4.905 \times 0.375 \\ &=88.29 \mathrm{N} \mathrm{m} \\ T &=I_{P} \alpha \\ \alpha &=\frac{T}{I_{p}}=\frac{88.29}{43}=2.053 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A bolt of major diameter 12 mm is required to clamp two steel plates. Cross sectional area of the threaded portion of the bolt is 84.3 [latex]mm^{2}[/latex]. The length of the threaded portion in grip is 30 mm, while the length of the unthreaded portion in grip is 8 mm. Young's modulus of material is 200 GPa. The effective stiffness (in MN/m) of the bolt in the clamped zone is _______

questions.question: A frame is subjected to a load P as shown in the figure. The frame has a constant flexural rigidity EI. The effect of axial load is neglected. The deflection at point A due to the applied load P is
questions.explanation: Bending moment in section AB [latex] \begin{aligned} M &=-P x \\ \frac{\partial M}{\partial P} &=-x \end{aligned}[/latex] Bending moment in section BC: [latex] \begin{aligned} M&=-P L\\ \frac{\partial M}{\partial P}&=-L \\ \delta_{A}&=\frac{1}{E I}\left[\int_{0}^{L}(-P x)(-x) d x+\int_{0}^{L}(-P L)(-L) d x\right] \\ \delta_{A}&=\frac{P}{E I}\left[\int_{0}^{L} x^{2} d x+L^{2} \int_{0}^{L} d x\right] \\ &=\frac{P}{E I}\left(\frac{L^{3}}{3}+L^{3}\right)=\frac{4 P L^{3}}{3 E I} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: A single degree of freedom system has a mass of 2 kg, stiffness 8 N/m and viscous damping  ratio 0.02. The dynamic magnification factor at an excitation frequency of 1.5 rad/s is  _______
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} M F&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\left[1-\left(\frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}\right)^{2}\right]^{2}+\left[2 \zeta \frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}\right]^{2}}}\\ \text{Given, } \omega&=1.5 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\ \omega_{n} &=\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}=\sqrt{\frac{8}{2}}=2 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\ \zeta &=0.02, \frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}=\frac{1.5}{2}=0.75 \\ \therefore \quad M F &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\left[1-(0.75)^{2}\right]^{2}+(2 \times 0.02 \times 0.75)^{2}}} \\ \therefore \quad M F &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{(0.4375)^{2}+(0.03)^{2}}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{0.1923}} \\ \therefore \quad M F &=2.28 \end{aligned}[/latex]

If the inner surface is at 1100[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and the outer surface is at 350[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C, then the design thickness (in meter) of the wall to maintain a steady heat flux of 2500 W/[latex]m^{2}[/latex] should be _______
questions.explanation: [latex] \begin{aligned} k&=1.15 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} ;\; T_{1}=1100^{o};\;T_{2}=350^{o}C\\ q&=2500 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2}\\ \mathrm{T}_{1}&=1100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}_{i}, T_{2}=350^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ Q&=\frac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{R_{t}} \\ \frac{Q}{A}&=\frac{k\left(T_{1}-T_{2}\right)}{\delta} \\ q&=\frac{k\left(T_{1}-T_{2}\right)}{\delta} \\ 2500&=\frac{1.15(1100-350)}{\delta} \\ \text{or}\quad \delta&=0.345 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: Two identical metal blocks L and M (specific heat = 0.4 kJ/kg.K), each having a mass of 5 kg, are initially at 313 K. A reversible refrigerator extracts heat from block L and rejects heat to block M until the temperature of block L reaches 293 K. The final temperature (in K) of block M is _______
questions.explanation: Given data: Specified heat, [latex] \begin{aligned} c&=0.4 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \text{ each body}\\ \text{Mass:}m&=5 \mathrm{kg} \quad \text { each body } \end{aligned}[/latex] Initial temperature, [latex] T_{1}=313 \mathrm{K} \quad \text { each body }[/latex] Final temprature of block L [latex] T_{2}=293 \mathrm{K}[/latex] Let [latex]\quad T_{f}=[/latex] Final temperature of block M, Entropy change of block L [latex] \Delta S_{L}=m c \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}[/latex] Entropy change of block M [latex] \Delta S_{M}=m c \log _{e} \frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}}[/latex] Entropy change of universe, [latex] \begin{aligned} \Delta S_{\text {univ }} &=\Delta S_{L}+\Delta S_{M} \\ &=mc \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}+mc \log _{e} \frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}} \end{aligned}[/latex] For a reversible refrigeration, [latex] \begin{aligned} \Delta S_{\text {univ }}&=0 \\ m c \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}&+m_{c} \log _{e} \frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}}=0\\ mc \log _{e} \frac{T_{2} T_{f}}{T_{1}^{2}}&=0\\ \text{or}\quad \log _{e} \frac{T_{2} T_{f}}{T_{1}^{2}}&=0\\ \text{or}\quad \frac{T_{2} T_{f}}{T_{1}^{2}} &=e^{0}=1 \\ T_{f} &=\frac{T_{1}^{2}}{T_{2}}=\frac{(313)^{2}}{293}=334.36 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given data:
Specified heat,
[latex] \begin{aligned} c&=0.4 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \text{ each body}\\ \text{Mass:}m&=5 \mathrm{kg} \quad \text { each body } \end{aligned}[/latex]
Initial temperature,
[latex] T_{1}=313 \mathrm{K} \quad \text { each body }[/latex]
Final temprature of block L
[latex] T_{2}=293 \mathrm{K}[/latex]
Let [latex]\quad T_{f}=[/latex] Final temperature of block M,
Entropy change of block L
[latex] \Delta S_{L}=m c \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}[/latex]
Entropy change of block M
[latex] \Delta S_{M}=m c \log _{e} \frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}}[/latex]
Entropy change of universe,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Delta S_{\text {univ }} &=\Delta S_{L}+\Delta S_{M} \\ &=mc \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}+mc \log _{e} \frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For a reversible refrigeration,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Delta S_{\text {univ }}&=0 \\ m c \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}&+m_{c} \log _{e} \frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}}=0\\ mc \log _{e} \frac{T_{2} T_{f}}{T_{1}^{2}}&=0\\ \text{or}\quad \log _{e} \frac{T_{2} T_{f}}{T_{1}^{2}}&=0\\ \text{or}\quad \frac{T_{2} T_{f}}{T_{1}^{2}} &=e^{0}=1 \\ T_{f} &=\frac{T_{1}^{2}}{T_{2}}=\frac{(313)^{2}}{293}=334.36 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: Steam with specific enthalpy (h) 3214 kJ/kg enters an adiabatic turbine operating at steady state with a flow rate 10 kg/s. As it expands, at a point where h is 2920 kJ/kg, 1.5 kg/s is extracted for heating purposes. The remaining 8.5 kg/s further expands to the turbine exit, where h = 2374 kJ/kg. Neglecting changes in kinetic and potential energies, the net power output (in kW) of the turbine   is _______
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} m_{1} &=10 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; \quad m_{2}=1.5 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; \quad m_{3}=8.5 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ h_{1} &=3214 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} ; \quad h_{2}=2920 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{3} &=2374 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ W_{T} &=m_{1}\left(h_{1}-h_{2}\right)+m_{3}\left(h_{2}-h_{3}\right) \\ &=10(3214-2920)+8.5(2920-2374) \\ &=7581 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} m_{1} &=10 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; \quad m_{2}=1.5 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; \quad m_{3}=8.5 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ h_{1} &=3214 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} ; \quad h_{2}=2920 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{3} &=2374 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ W_{T} &=m_{1}\left(h_{1}-h_{2}\right)+m_{3}\left(h_{2}-h_{3}\right) \\ &=10(3214-2920)+8.5(2920-2374) \\ &=7581 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: In a compression ignition engine, the inlet air pressure is 1 bar and the pressure at the end of isentropic compression is 32.42 bar. The expansion ratio is 8. Assuming ratio of specific heats ([latex]\gamma[/latex] ) as 1.4, the air standard efficiency (in percent) is _______
questions.explanation: Given, [latex]p_{1}=1[/latex] bar, [latex]p_{2}=32.42 [/latex] bar [latex] \begin{aligned} \gamma &=\frac{C_{p}}{c_{v}}=1.4 \\ \frac{V_{4}}{V_{3}} &=\frac{V_{1}}{V_{3}}=8 \end{aligned}[/latex] For process 1-2 [latex] \begin{aligned} p_{1} v_{1}^{\gamma}&=p_{2} v_{2}^{\gamma} \\ \therefore\left(\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}\right)^{\gamma}&=\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}=32.42 \\ \text { or } \quad \frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}} &=(32.42)^{1 / 1.4}=11.999 \approx 12 \\ r_{c} &=\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}=\frac{V_{1}}{8} \times \frac{12}{V_{1}}=1.5 \\ \eta_{\text {Diesel }} &=1-\frac{1}{r^{\gamma-1}}\left[\frac{r_{C}^{\gamma}-1}{\gamma\left(r_{C}-1\right)}\right] \\ &=1-\frac{1}{12^{0.4}}\left[\frac{1.5^{1.4}-1}{1.4 \times 0.5}\right] \\ &=0.596=59.6 \% \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given, [latex]p_{1}=1[/latex] bar, [latex]p_{2}=32.42 [/latex] bar
[latex] \begin{aligned} \gamma &=\frac{C_{p}}{c_{v}}=1.4 \\ \frac{V_{4}}{V_{3}} &=\frac{V_{1}}{V_{3}}=8 \end{aligned}[/latex]
For process 1-2
[latex] \begin{aligned} p_{1} v_{1}^{\gamma}&=p_{2} v_{2}^{\gamma} \\ \therefore\left(\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}\right)^{\gamma}&=\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}=32.42 \\ \text { or } \quad \frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}} &=(32.42)^{1 / 1.4}=11.999 \approx 12 \\ r_{c} &=\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}=\frac{V_{1}}{8} \times \frac{12}{V_{1}}=1.5 \\ \eta_{\text {Diesel }} &=1-\frac{1}{r^{\gamma-1}}\left[\frac{r_{C}^{\gamma}-1}{\gamma\left(r_{C}-1\right)}\right] \\ &=1-\frac{1}{12^{0.4}}\left[\frac{1.5^{1.4}-1}{1.4 \times 0.5}\right] \\ &=0.596=59.6 \% \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: At a work station, 5 jobs arrive every minute. The mean time spent on each job in the work station is 1/8 minute. The mean steady state number of jobs in the system is _______
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \lambda(\text { arrival rate })&=5 \text { jobs/minute } \\ \mu \text { (service rate) }&=8 \text { jobs/minute } \\ \qquad L_{S}&=\frac{\lambda}{\mu-\lambda}=\frac{5}{8-5}=\frac{5}{3}=1.67 \end{aligned}[/latex]
